harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created "Fleet Internal CA" on node1 via openssl (4096-bit RSA CA key, 10-year self-signed x509 CA cert). Issued a 2048-bit RSA server certificate for node2 (CN=node2, SAN=DNS:node2/IP:10.100.175.11) signed by the CA. Copied the CA cert, node2 cert, and node2 key to node2 via SSH/SCP, configured Apache httpd (mod_ssl) on node2 to listen on port 8443 with the issued certificate, opened firewalld port 8443, and verified TLS handshake succeeds with SSL_VERIFY:0 from node1. Installed the CA cert into the system trust store (/etc/pki/ca-trust + update-ca-trust) on both node1 and node2, confirmed via `trust list`. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id/service/data baselines, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially via systemctl reboot, confirmed each node's boot_id changed after reconnecting, and verified full recovery (httpd active, cert/key files intact, CA trust anchor present, firewall rule persisted, and cross-node HTTPS validation still succeeds).
actions_performed: Inspected OS/tooling on node1 and node2 (RHEL 9.8, openssl present)
Installed httpd + mod_ssl on node2
Built CA directory structure and openssl.cnf on node1
Generated CA private key and self-signed 'Fleet Internal CA' x509 cert on node1
Generated node2 key + CSR, signed it with the CA producing node2 server cert with SAN
Wired cluster SSH (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY, CLUSTER_HOSTS) between node1 and node2
Copied CA cert, node2 cert, and node2 key to node2 via scp
Edited /etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf on node2 to listen on 8443 and use the new cert/key/chain (recovered twice via dnf reinstall after a bad sed clobbered the file)
Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp on node2 and reloaded
Verified TLS handshake and cert validation from node1 using --cacert, then without it after trust install
Installed CA cert into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors on both nodes and ran update-ca-trust extract; confirmed via trust list
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baselines on both nodes
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery (CA trust, cert files, cross-node TLS check)
Rebooted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery (httpd active, cert/key files, CA trust, firewall rule, cross-node TLS check from node1)

evidence.requirement: CA 'Fleet Internal CA' created on node1
evidence.summary: openssl x509 output shows subject/issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA, O=Fleet Internal CA, valid 2026-2036

evidence.requirement: TLS certificate issued to node2 by the CA
evidence.summary: node2 cert shows Issuer: CN=Fleet Internal CA, Subject: CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.175.11

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with the issued certificate
evidence.summary: ssl.conf shows Listen 8443/VirtualHost :8443 pointing at fleet-ca cert/key/chain; httpd active and listening on 8443; firewall opened; curl TLS handshake from node1 succeeds with SSL_VERIFY:0

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor/authority on node1; curl without --cacert succeeds (SSL_VERIFY:0) confirming system trust store use

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node2
evidence.summary: trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor/authority on node2; local curl against node2's own service also verifies successfully

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=6bb7e004-1e2e-46ac-bfd7-fafa248a4e76, CA files present, trust anchor present

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proof
evidence.summary: connection timed out/reset during reboot, then reachable again with new boot_id=272b2cb1-6573-42f9-8bb0-77d43957246f (differs from baseline)

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: post-restart recovery proof
evidence.summary: post-reboot: CA cert/node2 cert files intact, trust anchor still present, cross-node HTTPS check to node2 still succeeds (SSL_VERIFY:0)

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6, httpd active, cert files present, HTTPS verify succeeds

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: changed boot identity proof
evidence.summary: connection timed out during reboot, then reachable again with new boot_id=cb1ef917-8087-415c-b939-0f3e20a81c58 (differs from baseline)

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: post-restart recovery proof
evidence.summary: post-reboot: httpd active, cert/key files intact, CA trust anchor present, firewall port 8443 persisted; cross-node curl from node1 succeeds with SSL_VERIFY:0
